queue.title: Exploration: what a loop actually is, and why its queue has never worked
queue.why: EXPLORATION ONLY -- the operator narrowed this run to 'ship the fixes... and run a explore on the loop and the side panel'. Do not implement. Recommend, do not decide anything that is the operator's.
queue.headline_finding: MEASURED DURING PREP, and it reframes the whole feature: Task.loop_id is READ in five places and WRITTEN in zero. tasks.py:427 (filter), scheduler.py:86 and :99 (stop-condition counts), scheduler.py:417 (event payload), schemas/jobs.py:71 (a comment). No code path sets it. Every test that exercises it fabricates the row directly in the ORM (test_scheduler.py:244, test_tasks.py:310-312) because no API would. CONSEQUENCE: the loop's queue -- the one thing that justifies Loop existing as a concept distinct from AIJob -- cannot be populated through any real path, and stop_when_queue_empties is therefore dead in production: _loop_stop_reason (scheduler.py:98-101) guards on ever_count, and a queue that can never be filled never trips it. VERIFY THIS INDEPENDENTLY before building the exploration on it.
must_cover: The unwritable queue above, verified independently, with the consequence for stop_when_queue_empties spelled out.

What writes Task.loop_id, if anything should. Options to weigh: create_loop takes an initial task list; the creating agent files tasks into its own loop; the first firing is a PLANNING firing that decomposes the goal into tasks. Each has a different governance story -- say which the operator can actually supervise.

What connects a firing to the queue. Today scheduler.py:296 _do_fire_job replays job.message verbatim and never looks at a task. Does a firing CLAIM the next task, or does the agent choose from the queue? This is upstream of the briefing.

Only then, the briefing: how a firing learns its position (purpose, what is done, what remains, what prior firings concluded), how it is capped so a long-running loop does not drown its own turn, and where it is assembled -- mirror how agents.py:1316 appends the charter to canonical context.

WHY Loop.charter_id is rejected (roadmap Proposal A). agents.py:1060-1064 builds the turn's charter from agent_row.charter_id; a loop already has an agent and that agent already has a charter, so a second one competes with no precedence rule. Operator's words: 'A loop or a job has an agent attached to it. This agent has a charter already.' Record the rejection so Proposal A does not resurface.

Field by field, what Loop legitimately holds vs AIJob + Agent: purpose (NO -- duplicates AIJob.name/message and the charter), stop_at / stop_when_queue_empties / stop_reason / stopped_at (YES -- a job runs forever, a loop terminates and records why), Task.loop_id (YES in principle -- see the headline finding). Defend the conclusion: a loop is not 'an agent on a schedule', because a bare AIJob is already exactly that. It is a job that ENDS and OWNS A BACKLOG.

The MCP gap: mcp_server.py:503-529 create_job exposes only name, agent, message, cron, session_mode, while jobs.py:93 _loop_opts_in means any one of purpose/stop_at/stop_when_queue_empties turns a job into a Loop. So an agent can create a job that runs forever and cannot create a loop that ends. Argue create_loop vs widening create_job; if it comes out even, prefer a separate tool (a distinct name teaches the concept exists; an optional argument hides it). The gate already exists -- jobs.py:21 _require_agent_job_allowance.

Governance questions the operator will care about, given they framed this as 'governance and visibility': can a loop's agent create another loop (runaway risk)? What bounds unattended spend? What happens when a firing fails, or the agent goes off-task? Raise them even where you cannot answer them.

The dangling-agent defect: AIJob.agent is a bare String(64), not an FK. scheduler.py:51-56 _job_agent_skip_reason returns None when NO agent row matches -- and None means PROCEED. Rename or archive an agent and its loops keep firing at a name nobody owns.

MINE THE REPO'S OWN DRIVER. .claude/autonomous/ is a WORKING implementation of exactly this feature, battle-tested across several multi-hour runs including one that died and recovered: STATE.json has a queue, a next_action written for a stranger, stop_at, stop_when_queue_empties, a heartbeat with a takeover grace, decisions_for_user, and a prose log. Map what that driver NEEDS against what Loop HAS, and let the gaps drive the design. This is the strongest evidence available and it is free. It is also the concrete path to Proposal C (the autonomous session as a Loop) -- note that, do not build it.

known_debts.summary: Task.loop_id is read in five places and written in ZERO -- tasks.py:427 (filter), scheduler.py:86/:99 (stop-condition counts), scheduler.py:417 (event payload), schemas/jobs.py:71 (a comment). No code path sets it; every test that exercises it fabricates the row directly in the ORM (test_scheduler.py:244, test_tasks.py:310-312). So a loop's queue cannot be populated through any real path, and stop_when_queue_empties is dead in production because _loop_stop_reason (scheduler.py:98-101) guards on ever_count, which can never become non-zero. Measured during prep 2026-08-18; Q5 must verify independently before relying on it.

hub/hub/main.py:84 ui_source_fingerprint folds `git status --porcelain` into the hash so uncommitted edits move it. But CLAUDE.md's documented workflow is build -> make ui -> commit TOGETHER, so the stamp is always recorded while the tree is dirty; the moment you commit, that dirty string empties and the fingerprint can never match again. Result: /health reports ui_stale on a bundle that is byte-for-byte correct. CONFIRMED this session -- commit 8898155 did rebuild and commit the assets, and a fresh rebuild produced byte-identical output with only the stamp changing (commit ab7e5fe). Fix shape: stamp from the committed tree, or exclude the dirty component from the recorded fingerprint while keeping it for the live check. Queued as Q8.

The Hub test fixture's sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory: resolves to a StaticPool -- ONE DBAPI connection shared by every session in the process -- so a concurrent session's close rolls back another's pending write while commit() still returns cleanly. Measured 105/200 commits lost with a concurrent poller vs 0/200 without. One test is xfailed for it. THREE attempts have failed: a file-backed DATABASE_URL hung the suite; session-scoped create_all produced 399 errors / 7 failures by skipping _run_alembic_upgrade(); a third attempt (file-backed + WAL + busy_timeout + session-scoped alembic) produced a NEW mode where pytest reports both an XPASS and an XFAIL for the same collected item. Do NOT attempt a fourth this run -- it is not on the queue and has eaten three sessions.

The Hub suite is near-100% fixture overhead -- create_app() plus drop_all/create_all across 43 tables per test is essentially all of its ~8-minute runtime. Entangled with staticpool-fixture-race; same warning applies.
CI has never run on master at 1e0d08e nor on any commit of autonomous/2026-08-18-the-app-feels-alive. Every suite result on record is local. Q1 exists to change this.
